reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch propose a scribal slip, the copyist's eye catching the 245 camels in the next verse, behind Nehemiah's higher singer count.

discrepancy.note: Paine's observation that Nehemiah's list differs from Ezra's in its particulars extends to the singers, tallied at 200 in one roster and 245 in the other.

quotes.text: Nehemiah, in like manner, gives a list of the returned families, and of the number of each family. He begins as in Ezra, by saying (vii. 8): "The children of Parosh, two thousand three hundred and seventy-two;" and so on through all the families. (The list differs in several of the particulars from that of Ezra.)
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), ch. I, on Ezra 2:65 and Nehemiah 7:67.
